court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court at Mumbai in Petition No. A-1711/2003
case_name: Mansi Mohan Chandarkar vs Mohan Vishnu Chandarkar
facts_of_case: The parties got married on 5/12/2001. The appellant started insisting to live separate and her general behaviour gave rise to a suspicion about her mental health. She was behaving arrogantly and insulting the family members of the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A party's mental condition can be inferred from their employment history.
legal_principles.held: The fact that the appellant was employed as a teacher from July 1999 to April 2002 would show that her mental condition was normal.

legal_principles.principle: A party's allegations of harassment must be substantiated by evidence.
legal_principles.held: It was contended that some time in March 2003 the appellant shifted to her parent's house as she was pregnant. She delivered a girl child on 25/5/2003, however the respondent did not come to see the appellant and the child and was not willing to take them to the matrimonial home.

outcome.final_order: The marriage between the parties is dissolved on the ground of cruelty under section 13(1) (i a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 with some other reliefs.
